news_analysis.retail_illusion: Retail investors panic-sell quality banking stocks and rush to buy overpriced out-of-the-money Put options fearing a systemic banking collapse.

comparison_data.myth: Retail buys overpriced OTM Puts fearing a systemic 2% Bank Nifty collapse.
comparison_data.reality: Institutions trigger stop-losses near 54,500, harvest inflated IV premiums, and re-accumulate banking equities.

stat_data.label: IV Expansion Penalty
stat_data.context: Buying naked options during a 2% intraday crash forces retail buyers to pay up to 40% inflated Implied Volatility premiums. When the market stabilizes, IV crush annihilates options value even if direction is correct.

slides.title: How Desks Extract Retail Liquidity
flowchart_data: 1. Engineer a sharp 2% index drop toward key visual support at 54,500.
2. Trigger retail stop-loss orders and spike Implied Volatility (IV) to peak levels.
3. Sell overpriced options premium to panic buyers while absorbing cheap underlying shares.

slides.title: The Mathematical Drag Of IV
slides.card_text: When Bank Nifty drops near 54,500, implied volatility surges instantly. Retail traders buy naked OTM options at peak prices. The moment index movement slows down, theta decay combined with IV crush destroys 30% to 50% of premium value within hours.

slides.title: The Unbreakable Hedging Rule
slides.card_text: Never purchase unhedged naked index options during an intraday spike in volatility. Institutional desks wait for Implied Volatility (IV) expansion to exhaust itself before executing defined-risk spread strategies or re-accumulating core positions.

checklist_data.text: Buying naked OTM Puts after a 2% drop when IV is overextended.
Executing hedged spreads (e.g., Put Vertical Spread) to offset volatility decay.
Waiting for IV rank to contract before taking directional trend trades.
